correctness.rationale: The length-three chains split by ordered opposite-part endpoints. At a matched pair the image identifies labels along the off-matching bipartite relation graph on 2(n−1) labels, so the augmented quotient is free of rank one for n=3 and zero for n≥4; at distinct indices each generator is individually a boundary. At length four the three degree-three step patterns are (1,1,2), (1,2,1), (2,1,1); the degree-four steps are all 1. Direct deletion gives the signs and indicator conditions in (1)–(2). The degree-three differential is onto degree two by the listed pivot tuples (at distinct endpoints P_{b,a}↦Y, R_{b,a}↦−Z, P_{b,k}↦Y−X_k). For coincident endpoints the cocycle relations kill Q and leave only the X_k coboundaries. For distinct endpoints these pivots normalize away the coboundaries over an arbitrary abelian group: k=a or b in the degree-four relations eliminates the listed classes, and for each k∈S a second l∈S kills the remaining R_{k,l}, P_{l,k}, R_{k,a}, Q_{b,a}. When |S|=1 the two residual coefficients have only the equality R_{k,a}=Q_{b,a}; the cohomology functor is naturally the coefficient group. Since H₂ at length four is zero, universal coefficients identify these functors with Hom of the sought integral H₃ and exclude torsion. Thus n=3 has 6 matched and 12 distinct ordered same-part classes in the respective bidegrees; n≥4 has none contributing. The distance table also proves each three-index six-cycle is isometric and its map has zero target. Independent bounded Smith checks verify chain composition and endpoint ranks for n=3,4,5; those checks do not prove the all-n statement.
residual_risks: No conclusion about higher bidegrees or full diagonality.
